:::{#thm-arithmetic-prefix-code}
#### Arithmetic codes are prefix codes

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv)
whose values each have [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability).
Then the codewords of the [arithmetic code](#def-arithmetic-code) for $n$ [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) copies of $X$
form a [prefix code](huffman-codes.qmd#def-prefix-code) on the messages of length $n$.

:::

::: {.proof}

Let $x$ be a message,
let $[a, a + w)$ be its final slice,
and let $m = a + w/2$.
Write $k = \codelenf{x}$,
and let $t$ be the number whose [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) after the point are $c(x)$.
Truncating $m$ to $k$ digits gives

$$t \le m < t + 2^{-k}.$$

Because $k \ge -\log_2 w + 1$,
we have $2^{-k} \le w/2$.
So $t > m - 2^{-k} \ge m - w/2 = a$,
and $t + 2^{-k} \le m + w/2 = a + w$.
This shows that the slice $[t, t + 2^{-k})$,
which holds the numbers whose [bits](entropy.qmd#def-bit) begin with $c(x)$,
lies inside the final slice of $x$.

Suppose that $c(x)$ were the beginning of $c(x')$ for two different messages $x$ and $x'$.
Every number whose digits begin with $c(x')$ also begins with $c(x)$,
so the slice of $c(x')$ lies inside the slice of $c(x)$.
The first lies inside the final slice of $x'$,
and the second inside the final slice of $x$,
so these two final slices would share a point.
@lem-arithmetic-interval rules that out,
so no codeword is the beginning of another.

:::
